q: Who proposed the Artificial System of classification?
The Artificial System, based on superficial morphological characters, was given by Linnaeus.
The Natural System of classification was proposed by:
George Bentham and Joseph Dalton Hooker proposed the Natural System.
The Phylogenetic System of classification is based on:
The Phylogenetic System, given by Englar and Prantl, is based on evolutionary relationships.
Numerical Taxonomy assigns to each character:
In numerical taxonomy, all observable characters are given numbers and codes, easily processed by computers.
According to the chapter, Plantae is now described under how many major groups?
Plantae is described under 5 groups: Algae, Bryophytes, Pteridophytes, Gymnosperms, and Angiosperms.
Which system of classification is based on evolutionary relationship between organisms?
Phylogenetic classification is explicitly based on evolutionary relationships.
Which of these is a unicellular alga?
Chlamydomonas is unicellular; Volvox is colonial, Ulothrix and Spirogyra are filamentous.
Which alga is colonial in form?
Volvox is a colonial form of algae.
Vegetative reproduction in algae typically occurs by:
Vegetative reproduction is by fragmentation; each fragment develops into a thallus.
Asexual reproduction in algae is by the production of:
Asexual reproduction is by flagellated (motile) zoospores.
Fusion of two similar, non-motile gametes (as in Spirogyra) is called:
Isogamous reproduction involves fusion of similar gametes, motile or non-motile.
Fusion of a large, non-motile female gamete with a smaller, motile male gamete is termed:
This is oogamous reproduction, e.g. in Volvox and Fucus.
Anisogamous reproduction, as seen in some species of Chlamydomonas, involves gametes that are:
Anisogamous reproduction is the fusion of two gametes dissimilar in size.
Agar, used to grow microbes and in ice-creams and jellies, is obtained from:
Agar is obtained from the red algae Gelidium and Gracilaria.
Which marine algae are used directly as food?
Species of Sargassum, Laminaria, and Porphyra are marine algae used as food.
Lichens are formed by an association of algae with:
Some algae occur in association with fungi, forming lichens.
Algae are divided into how many main classes?
Algae are divided into three main classes: Chlorophyceae, Phaeophyceae, and Rhodophyceae.
Chlorophyceae members are commonly called green algae.
Phaeophyceae members are commonly called brown algae.
Rhodophyceae members are commonly called red algae due to the pigment r-phycoerythrin.
Pyrenoids, found in most Chlorophyceae chloroplasts, are storage bodies containing:
Pyrenoids are storage bodies containing proteins in addition to starch.
Food in Phaeophyceae is typically stored as:
Phaeophyceae store food as complex carbohydrates such as laminarin or mannitol.
The gelatinous coating on the cellulosic cell wall of brown algae is made of:
Vegetative cells of brown algae have a cellulosic wall covered by a gelatinous coating of algin.
In a brown alga's plant body, the leaf-like photosynthetic organ is called the:
The frond is the leaf-like photosynthetic organ; the stipe is the stalk and the holdfast attaches to the substratum.
Red algae store food as Floridean starch, similar in structure to amylopectin and glycogen.
The red pigment characteristic of Rhodophyceae is:
Rhodophyceae contain the red pigment r-phycoerythrin along with chlorophyll a and d.
Sexual reproduction in Rhodophyceae is characteristically:
Sexual reproduction in red algae is oogamous, with complex post-fertilisation development.
Ectocarpus, Dictyota, Laminaria, Sargassum, and Fucus all belong to which class?
These are all examples of Phaeophyceae (brown algae).
Polysiphonia, Gelidium, Gracilaria, and Porphyra all belong to which class?
These genera are all examples of Rhodophyceae (red algae).
Chara, Volvox, and Ulothrix are examples of which algal class?
Chara, Volvox, and Ulothrix are Chlorophyceae (green algae) examples.
The bryophyte plant body is haploid and is called the gametophyte.
The male sex organ in bryophytes is called:
The male sex organ, producing biflagellate antherozoids, is the antheridium.
The female sex organ in bryophytes is called:
The flask-shaped female sex organ, producing a single egg, is the archegonium.
Bryophytes are attached to the substratum by:
Bryophytes are attached by unicellular or multicellular rhizoids, lacking true roots.
Antherozoids released from the antheridium reach the archegonium through:
Antherozoids are released into water, through which they travel to reach the archegonium.
Bryophytes usually occur in cool, damp, and shady areas due to their dependence on water for reproduction.
The bryophyte sex organs (antheridia and archegonia) are described as:
The sex organs in bryophytes are multicellular structures.
Bryophytes are divided into which two classes?
Bryophytes comprise two classes: Liverworts and Mosses.
Marchantia is a classic example of a:
Funaria, Polytrichum, and Sphagnum are examples of:
These three genera are classic examples of mosses.
Gemmae in liverworts develop in specialised structures called:
Gemmae are green, multicellular asexual buds that develop in gemma cups on the thallus.
The first stage in moss gametophyte development, arising directly from a spore, is the:
The protonema stage develops directly from the spore as a creeping, green, branched, filamentous structure.
In mosses, antheridia and archegonia are produced at:
The apex of the leafy shoots
Antheridia and archegonia are produced at the apex of the leafy shoots in mosses.
The moss sporophyte, more elaborate than in liverworts, consists of foot, seta, and capsule.
Peat, used as fuel, is obtained from which moss?
Peat provided by Sphagnum is used as fuel.
Sphagnum is used as packing material during transport of living material because of its:
Sphagnum's high water-holding capacity makes it useful as packing material in trans-shipment of living material.
Mosses along with lichens form the pioneer community in:
Mosses along with lichens form the pioneer community in land and desert succession.
Which structure is unique to mosses and not found in the liverwort life cycle as described?
The protonema stage, arising directly from the spore, is a moss-specific developmental phase not described for liverworts.
The dominant phase in the pteridophyte life cycle is the:
Unlike bryophytes, the sporophyte is the dominant phase in pteridophytes.
Small leaves in Selaginella are called:
Small leaves, as in Selaginella, are called microphylls.
Sporophylls are leaves associated with sporangia.
The free-living, photosynthetic gametophyte of pteridophytes is called the:
The prothallus is the small, multicellular, free-living gametophyte of pteridophytes.
Plants producing spores that are all of a similar kind are called:
Homosporous plants produce spores that are all of a similar kind.
Selaginella and Salvinia are examples of plants that are:
Selaginella and Salvinia produce two kinds of spores — megaspores and microspores — making them heterosporous.
In heterosporous pteridophytes, the megaspore germinates to give rise to a:
Megaspores germinate to give rise to female gametophytes; microspores give rise to male gametophytes.
Compact structures formed by sporophylls in Selaginella, Lycopodium, and Equisetum are called:
Sporophylls in these genera form distinct, compact structures called strobili or cones.
Which class of Pteridophyta includes the whisk fern Psilotum?
Psilotum belongs to class Psilopsida (whisk ferns).
Which class of Pteridophyta includes the horsetail Equisetum?
Dryopteris, Pteris, Adiantum, Salvinia, and Marsilea belong to which class of Pteridophyta?
These fern genera belong to class Pteropsida.
Which class includes Selaginella and Lycopodium (club mosses)?
Selaginella and Lycopodium belong to class Lycopsida (club mosses).
Sporangia in pteridophytes produce spores through:
Sporangia produce spores by meiosis occurring in spore mother cells.
Large leaves found in ferns are called:
Large leaves, as seen in ferns, are called macrophylls.
The world's largest gymnosperm plant mentioned in the chapter is:
Sequoia, the giant redwood, is described as the world's largest plant among gymnosperms.
Mycorrhiza is a symbiotic association of fungi with the roots of:
Mycorrhiza shows association of fungi with Pinus roots.
Coralloid roots, associated with N2-fixing cyanobacteria, are found in:
Coralloid roots of Cycas show association with nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria.
Gymnosperms are heterosporous, producing both microspores and megaspores.
In which gymnosperm genus do male and female strobili occur on the same tree?
In Pinus, male and female strobili may be borne on the same tree.
In which gymnosperm genus do male and female strobili occur on different trees?
In Cycas, male and female strobili occur on different (separate) trees.
A microspore in gymnosperms develops into a reduced male gametophyte generation known as the:
The reduced male gametophyte confined to a few cells, developing within the microsporangium, is the pollen grain.
The megaspore mother cell in gymnosperms is a differentiated cell of the:
The megaspore mother cell is a differentiated cell of the nucellus.
The nucellus protected by envelopes in gymnosperms is known as the:
Nucellus protected by envelopes is known as an ovule.
How many megaspores are typically formed when the megaspore mother cell divides meiotically?
The megaspore mother cell divides meiotically to form four megaspores.
The female gametophyte in gymnosperms bears two or more of which structure?
The multicellular female gametophyte bears two or more archegonia, remaining within the megasporangium.
How is pollen typically transferred to the ovule in gymnosperms?
Pollen grains released from the microsporangium are carried by air currents to the ovule.
In angiosperms, pollen grains and ovules develop within specialised structures called:
Unlike gymnosperms, angiosperm pollen grains and ovules develop in flowers.
In angiosperms, seeds are enclosed in:
In angiosperms, the seeds are enclosed in fruits.
The smallest angiosperm mentioned in the chapter is:
Wolffia is cited as the smallest angiosperm, in contrast to tall trees like Eucalyptus.
A tall angiosperm tree, over 100 metres, mentioned in the chapter is:
Eucalyptus trees can grow over 100 metres, illustrating the size range of angiosperms.
After fertilisation in angiosperms, the ovary typically develops into the:
The ovary develops into the fruit, which encloses the seed(s).
Which algal association with animals is mentioned in the chapter?
The chapter mentions algae occurring in association with animals, such as on sloth bear.
Which algal class includes species that can form dense green mats in ponds?
Chlorophyceae (green algae) commonly forms dense green mats in freshwater bodies like ponds.
Which of these is NOT a correct pairing of alga and its class?
Spirogyra belongs to Chlorophyceae, not Phaeophyceae; the other pairings are correct.
In bryophytes, which generation is genetically identical to the spores that produced it?
Spores are haploid and germinate directly into the haploid gametophyte, making them genetically continuous with it.
Which structure in bryophytes is described as flask-shaped?
The archegonium, the female sex organ, is flask-shaped and produces a single egg.
Which structure allows liverworts to reproduce asexually apart from fragmentation?
Liverworts reproduce asexually via gemmae, formed in gemma cups on the thallus.
Mosses and lichens together are described in the chapter as the pioneer community in:
Mosses along with lichens form the pioneer community in land and desert succession.
In pteridophytes, sporangia develop in association with leaves called:
Sporangia develop in association with leaves called sporophylls.
Which pteridophyte class is characterised by jointed stems and is commonly called horsetails?
Sphenopsida, represented by Equisetum, is commonly known as horsetails.
Which gymnosperm is described as a 'living fossil'?
Ginkgo, placed in Coniferopsida, is described as a living fossil.
Angiosperms are also known by which common name?
Angiosperms are commonly known as flowering plants.
Which of these products is NOT listed in the chapter as being provided by angiosperms?
Angiosperms provide food, fodder, fuel, medicines, and other commercial products — but their seeds are enclosed in fruit, not naked.
Aristotle classified plants into trees, shrubs and:
Aristotle's morphology-based system grouped plants as trees, shrubs, and herbs.
Whittaker's Five Kingdom classification was proposed in:
R.H. Whittaker proposed the Five Kingdom classification in 1969.
Which of these is NOT one of Whittaker's five kingdoms?
Viruses are acellular and are not included in Whittaker's Five Kingdom system.
Bentham and Hooker's Natural System added which character NOT used by the Artificial System?
The Natural System added embryology, anatomy, phytochemistry and more beyond superficial morphology.
Cladistics traces characters back to a group's:
Cladistics uses shared derived characters traceable to the most recent common ancestor.
Plantae is now recognised as consisting of how many major groups?
Plantae is now divided into Algae, Bryophytes, Pteridophytes, Gymnosperms and Angiosperms.
Cyanobacteria are excluded from 'algae' today because they belong to:
Cyanobacteria are prokaryotic and classified under Monera, not Plantae.
A classification system based purely on coded, computer-processed characters is:
Numerical Taxonomy assigns numeric codes to all characters for computer processing.
Which system is explicitly based on evolutionary relationships between organisms?
The Phylogenetic System, given by Englar and Prantl, is based on evolutionary relationships.
Which of these is a filamentous alga?
Spirogyra is a classic filamentous green alga.
In oogamous reproduction, the female gamete is:
Oogamy involves a large, non-motile female gamete fusing with a small, motile male gamete.
Vegetative reproduction in algae is typically by fragmentation of the thallus.
Chlorella and Spirulina are valued as food supplements mainly because they are:
Both are protein-rich unicellular algae, compact enough to be called 'space food'.
Lichens are formed by a symbiotic association between algae and:
Lichens are a symbiotic association of algae (or cyanobacteria) with fungi.
Marine algae such as Sargassum and Porphyra are economically important mainly as:
Sargassum, Laminaria, and Porphyra are used directly as food.
Algae are divided into how many main classes based on pigmentation?
Algae are divided into three classes: Chlorophyceae, Phaeophyceae, Rhodophyceae.
Chlorophyceae are commonly known as green algae.
The gelatinous coating on the brown algal cell wall is made of:
Brown algae have a cellulosic wall coated with the gelatinous substance algin.
Which pigment is characteristic of Rhodophyceae?
r-phycoerythrin is the red pigment characteristic of Rhodophyceae.
Pyrenoids, found in Chlorophyceae chloroplasts, store:
Pyrenoids are storage bodies containing protein in addition to starch.
A marine alga with holdfast, stipe and frond that stores food as mannitol belongs to:
Holdfast-stipe-frond anatomy and mannitol storage are diagnostic of Phaeophyceae.
Chlorophyceae cell walls have an inner layer of cellulose and an outer layer of:
The Chlorophyceae wall has an inner cellulose layer and an outer pectose layer.
Ectocarpus and Dictyota are examples of which algal class?
Ectocarpus and Dictyota are examples of Phaeophyceae (brown algae).
Zoospores of Phaeophyceae are typically described as:
Phaeophyceae zoospores are biflagellate, pear-shaped, with two unequal laterally attached flagella.
The dominant phase of the bryophyte life cycle is the:
The haploid gametophyte is the dominant, independent phase in bryophytes.
Antherozoids released by the antheridium travel to the archegonium through:
Antherozoids are flagellated and must swim through a film of water to reach the egg.
Bryophytes attach to the substratum using:
Bryophytes lack true roots and attach via uni/multicellular rhizoids.
The zygote in bryophytes develops into a:
The zygote grows into a multicellular sporophyte without immediate meiosis.
Bryophyte sex organs (antheridia and archegonia) are:
Both antheridia and archegonia are multicellular structures.
Gemmae, the asexual reproductive structures of liverworts, form in:
Gemmae are green, multicellular buds formed in gemma cups on the liverwort thallus.
The first stage of moss gametophyte development, arising directly from the spore, is the:
The protonema is the filamentous first stage developing directly from the spore.
In mosses, sex organs develop at the:
Antheridia and archegonia form at the apex of the leafy shoots in mosses.
Peat, used as fuel, is obtained from which moss genus?
Sphagnum peat is economically used as fuel.
Sphagnum's usefulness as packing material for living specimens is due to its:
Sphagnum's high water-holding capacity makes it ideal packing material.
Mosses together with lichens form the pioneer community in:
Mosses and lichens are pioneer colonisers in land/desert ecological succession.
Pteridophytes are evolutionarily significant as the first plants with:
Pteridophytes are the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissue (xylem and phloem).
Small leaves as seen in Selaginella are called:
Small leaves such as in Selaginella are termed microphylls.
The free-living gametophyte of a pteridophyte is called the:
The prothallus is the free-living, photosynthetic gametophyte of pteridophytes.
Compact structures formed by sporophylls in Selaginella and Equisetum are called:
These compact sporophyll structures are known as strobili or cones.
Psilotum belongs to which class of Pteridophyta?
Psilotum, the whisk fern, belongs to class Psilopsida.
Equisetum, the horsetail, belongs to class:
Dryopteris, Pteris and Adiantum all belong to class:
These fern genera all belong to class Pteropsida.
Sporangia in pteridophytes produce spores via:
Spores form through meiosis occurring in spore mother cells within the sporangia.
Mycorrhiza is a symbiotic fungal association found with the roots of:
Mycorrhiza shows fungal association specifically with Pinus roots.
In which gymnosperm genus do male and female strobili occur on separate trees?
In Cycas, male and female strobili occur on different (separate) trees.
The megaspore mother cell divides meiotically to form how many megaspores?
The megaspore mother cell divides meiotically to form four megaspores.
Pollen in gymnosperms is typically transferred to the ovule by:
Gymnosperm pollination characteristically occurs via air currents (wind).
Gymnosperms are classified into how many classes?
Gymnosperms are classified into three classes: Cycadopsida, Coniferopsida, Gnetopsida.
Angiosperm seeds are enclosed in fruits, developed from the ovary.
Which structure is unique to angiosperms among the five plant groups discussed?
The flower is unique to angiosperms among the five groups covered.
Angiosperms are also commonly known as:
Angiosperms are commonly known as flowering plants.
A tree shows coralloid roots hosting nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria. This tree is most likely:
Coralloid roots with N2-fixing cyanobacteria are characteristic of Cycas.
The ______ System of classification was proposed by Bentham and Hooker.
The Natural System was proposed by Bentham and Hooker.
______ is based on chromosome number, structure, and behaviour.
Fusion of two gametes similar in size is called ______ reproduction.
Isogamous reproduction involves gametes similar in size.
Agar is obtained from the algal genera Gelidium and ______.
Agar is obtained from Gelidium and Gracilaria.
Green algae (Chlorophyceae) owe their colour to chlorophyll a and ______.
Chlorophyceae contain chlorophyll a and b.
In brown algae, the leaf-like photosynthetic organ is called the ______.
The frond is the leaf-like photosynthetic organ in brown algae.
The male sex organ in bryophytes, called the ______, produces biflagellate antherozoids.
The antheridium is the male sex organ producing antherozoids.
The green, multicellular asexual buds in liverworts are called ______.
Gemmae are the asexual buds formed in gemma cups on liverwort thalli.
The creeping, filamentous first stage of the moss gametophyte is called the ______.
The protonema is the first, filamentous stage of the moss gametophyte.
The free-living gametophyte of pteridophytes is called the ______.
The prothallus is the free-living gametophyte of pteridophytes.
Plants producing two kinds of spores — micro and mega — are called ______.
Heterosporous plants produce microspores and megaspores.
The symbiotic root association of fungi with Pinus is called ______.
Mycorrhiza is the fungal association with Pinus roots.
In angiosperms, seeds develop enclosed within the ______.
Angiosperm seeds are enclosed within fruits, formed from the ovary.
Angiosperms are divided into dicotyledons and ______.
Angiosperms are divided into dicotyledons and monocotyledons.
Fusion of two dissimilar-sized gametes is called ______ reproduction.
Anisogamous reproduction involves fusion of gametes dissimilar in size.
The pigment r-phycoerythrin is characteristic of ______.
r-phycoerythrin is the red pigment characteristic of Rhodophyceae.
The ______ System of classification was given by Linnaeus.
The Artificial System, based on superficial morphology, was given by Linnaeus.
The bryophyte sporophyte remains attached to and dependent on the ______ for food.
The sporophyte remains attached to and dependent on the gametophyte for nutrition.
Mosses and ______ together form the pioneer community in land succession.
Mosses along with lichens form the pioneer community in land and desert succession.
Sporophylls in Selaginella and Equisetum form compact structures called ______.
Compact sporophyll structures in these genera are called strobili or cones.
The world's largest gymnosperm plant is ______, the giant redwood.
Sequoia, the giant redwood, is the world's largest gymnosperm plant mentioned in the chapter.
Angiosperm ovules develop within the ______, unlike naked gymnosperm ovules.
Angiosperm ovules develop enclosed within the ovary.
The hydrocolloid Carrageen is obtained from ______ algae.
Carrageen is a hydrocolloid obtained from red algae (Rhodophyceae).
The Phylogenetic System of classification was proposed by ______.
The Phylogenetic System was given by Englar and Prantl.
The vegetative reproduction mode common to most algae is ______.
Vegetative reproduction in algae is typically by fragmentation.
Brown algae (Phaeophyceae) store food mainly as laminarin or ______.
Phaeophyceae store food as laminarin or mannitol.
The female sex organ in bryophytes, which produces a single egg, is the ______.
The archegonium is the flask-shaped female sex organ producing the egg.
The moss sporophyte consists of foot, seta and ______.
The moss sporophyte comprises foot, seta and capsule.
Large leaves seen in ferns are called ______.
Large fern leaves are called macrophylls.
Gymnosperms are classified into three classes: Cycadopsida, Coniferopsida and ______.
The third gymnosperm class is Gnetopsida.
After fertilisation in angiosperms, the ovary develops into the ______.
The ovary develops into the fruit after fertilisation.
Cyanobacteria are excluded from 'algae' since they belong to Kingdom ______.
Cyanobacteria are prokaryotic and belong to Monera.
Agar, used to culture microbes, is obtained from red algae such as Gelidium and ______.
Agar comes from Gelidium and Gracilaria.
The Artificial System of classification was proposed by:
The Artificial System, based on superficial vegetative and androecium characters, was given by Linnaeus.
George Bentham and Joseph Dalton Hooker proposed the Natural System of classification.
Chemotaxonomy classifies plants based on their:
Chemotaxonomy uses the chemical constituents of a plant to resolve taxonomic doubts.
Algae are chlorophyll-bearing, thalloid and autotrophic organisms.
Vegetative reproduction in algae mainly occurs by:
Vegetative reproduction in algae occurs by fragmentation, with each fragment growing into a new thallus.
Fusion of two similar-sized motile gametes is called:
Isogamy is the fusion of two gametes similar in size and motility, as in Chlamydomonas.
Agar, used to culture microbes, is obtained from the red algae Gelidium and Gracilaria.
The stored food in Phaeophyceae is:
Phaeophyceae store food as complex carbohydrates such as laminarin or mannitol.
Which of these is an example of Phaeophyceae?
Ectocarpus is a well-known example of Phaeophyceae (brown algae).
Bryophytes are called the amphibians of the plant kingdom because they:
Bryophytes live on land but require water for the antherozoids to swim to the archegonium and fertilize the egg.
The dominant phase in the life cycle of a bryophyte is the:
In bryophytes, the haploid gametophyte is the dominant, independent phase.
The male sex organ in bryophytes is called the:
The antheridium is the male sex organ in bryophytes, producing biflagellate antherozoids.
Peat, used as fuel, is obtained from:
Sphagnum, a moss, yields peat which is used as a fuel.
Marchantia is a well-known example of the Liverworts class of Bryophyta.
Gemmae are found in specialized structures called:
Gemmae are green, multicellular asexual buds produced in gemma cups on the thallus of liverworts.
Funaria is a well-known example of:
Funaria is a common example of the moss class of Bryophyta.
Pteridophytes were the first plants to possess:
Pteridophytes were the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissue (xylem and phloem).
The dominant phase in pteridophytes is the:
The dominant phase in pteridophytes is the diploid sporophyte.
Selaginella and Salvinia are examples of pteridophytes that are:
Selaginella and Salvinia are heterosporous, producing both microspores and megaspores.
The free-living photosynthetic gametophyte of a fern is called the:
The prothallus is the small, free-living, photosynthetic gametophyte of pteridophytes.
Coralloid roots, associated with nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria, are found in:
Coralloid roots showing symbiotic association with N2-fixing cyanobacteria are found in Cycas.
In angiosperms, the seeds are enclosed within the:
In angiosperms, following fertilization, seeds develop enclosed within a fruit.
Angiosperms are divided into two classes, namely:
Angiosperms are classified into two classes: the Dicotyledons and the Monocotyledons.
The smallest known flowering plant is:
Wolffia is the smallest known flowering plant.
Pollen grains and ovules in angiosperms develop within:
In angiosperms, pollen grains and ovules develop within specialized reproductive structures called flowers.
The vegetative growth in algae occurs mainly by:
Vegetative growth in algae occurs through cell division, and fragmentation is a common asexual reproductive method in filamentous forms.
In bryophytes, the dominant, photosynthetic phase of the life cycle is the:
In bryophytes, the gametophyte is the dominant, free-living, photosynthetic phase, while the sporophyte remains attached to and dependent on it.
Floridean starch is the stored food of:
Brown algae (Phaeophyceae) cell walls contain algin.
Selaginella and Salvinia are heterosporous — precursor to the seed habit.
The dominant phase in bryophytes is:
Coralloid roots with N₂-fixing cyanobacteria are found in:
Liverwort Marchantia — gemmae in gemma cups.

Fucus is diplontic; Ectocarpus is haplo-diplontic.
